messages:
Maya Patel: Hey all — I'm Maya, new shadow for this week. Can someone confirm tonight's primary/secondary and any coverage gaps? I'm available 17:00-01:00 PT. Also want the quick runbook pointer and any tips about noisy alerts. Thanks!

Leon Wu: hi @Maya Patel — welcome! Primary tonight is Samir (primary), I'm secondary until 22:00 PT, then Rachel takes over as secondary. Coverage gap note: we only have one EU responder overnight, but that's expected.

Samir Khan: @Maya Patel welcome aboard. Primary = me. Secondary schedule: Leon until 22:00, then Rachel. If you want to shadow a live page, easiest window is 18:00-21:00 PT — we historically get most flakey traffic then.

Maya Patel: awesome, thanks. where's the pared-down runbook i should keep in my head?

Leon Wu: quick runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-quickstart (bookmark it). Short checklist: ack, assess impact, run `diagnose.sh` on the gateway pod, open an incident if >10% error rate or latency SLO breach.

Rachel O'Neill: a couple of practical tips for shadowing: 1) Read the `pager-noise` section, it explains common false-positive patterns, 2) watch KV cache thrashing alerts — they look like CPU spikes but correlate with a recent rollout.

Oncall Bot: Incident Alert: inference-gateway CPU spike detected (node: gpu-2a) — 91% for 3m — severity: sev3 — page routed to: samir@pager (ack required)

Samir Khan: acked. I'm checking logs now. Maya, if you want to watch the console I'll paste the sequence I run.

Maya Patel: watching now.

Samir Khan: steps I run (copy+paste):
```
# step 1: see pods and recent restarts
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep gateway
kubectl -n inference describe pod gateway-*** | egrep "Events|OOMKilled|BackOff"
# step 2: tail logs
kubectl -n inference logs -f deployment/gateway --since=10m
# step 3: check metrics
curl -s "http://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total[5m])"
```

Leon Wu: also check `rolling-m deployments` page — if a release hit 16:50, correlate. For paging thresholds: if error_rate > 5% sustained for 5m OR latency p95 > 2s sustained for 5m, we create an incident. For CPU spikes alone, follow mitigation steps first (scale/evict) before declaring broad customer impact.

Maya Patel: got it. If I see the same alert while Samir is busy, should I escalate to Leon or open the incident channel?

Samir Khan: if I'm the primary and unresponsive >5 min, first ping the secondary (Leon) and then open an incident if impact criteria met. Use `#incidents` channel for public incidents.

Rachel O'Neill: for shadowing tasks this week: you should practice an ack+diagnose and then a simulated handoff. We'll run a mock page tomorrow 09:30 PT. I'll add you to the rota for that.

Maya Patel: appreciate that. Any admin steps I need before I can ack pages? MFA? Pager access?

Leon Wu: ensure you have PagerDuty invited and your device registered. If you don't have the PD invite, DM @security-ops. Also set your contact hours on PD to show availability 17:00-01:00 PT.

Oncall Bot: Reminder: New shadow policy requires you to shadow at least two live pages and complete the shadow checklist before independent acking is allowed. Checklist link: https://redwood.internal/oncall/shadow-checklist

Maya Patel: thanks for the checklist link — I'll start that. Any reusable snippets I should memorize?

Samir Khan: memorize these responses: `We're investigating, no confirmed customer impact yet.` and `Mitigation in progress: scaling gateway replicas / draining node` — helps keep comms consistent.

Leon Wu: runbook excerpt for quick mitigation (paste into notes):
```
1) If CPU >90% and traffic spike: scale gateway by +2 replicas: kubectl -n inference scale deployment/gateway --replicas=$(current+2)
2) If KV cache thrash suspected: temporarily flip config `cache.bypass=true` via /ops/configs and monitor
3) If rollout suspected: rollback last deployment: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/gateway --to-revision=<prev>`
```

Maya Patel: noted. For handoffs, what exact words do we use? I want to practice the handoff script.

Rachel O'Neill: handoff script (two lines): `Handoff: primary Samir -> Maya (shadow), state: investigating CPU spike, mitigation: scaled +2, monitoring.` Then secondary Leon adds: `Secondary: Leon -> Rachel at 22:00 PT; no outstanding incidents.` Keep it short in the thread and paste longer notes to the incident ticket.

Samir Khan: example handoff I'll post at 21:58 before my shift ends tonight. Maya, you'll be included as shadow in that message. Please ack and confirm when you understand.

Maya Patel: will do. One more: any common gotchas for new shadows?

Leon Wu: yeah — don't assume every CPU spike needs an incident; check recent rollouts and control-plane logs first. Also don't fiddle with runbooks' ops steps unless a senior says so. Ask first.

Rachel O'Neill: and don't forget to log your shadow steps in the onboarding doc so we can sign off. I added you to the doc.

Maya Patel: thanks everyone — feeling better. I'll wait for Samir's handoff tonight and join the mock page tomorrow morning. :raised_hands:

Oncall Bot: Scheduled mock page: 2024-05-02T09:30:00Z — organizer: Rachel O'Neill — channel: #eng-oncall
